title: Product Usage Scoring & Routing
description: An explainable weekly Sales and Customer Success routing system that separates fit, product usage, and buying intent, then syncs one approved action to HubSpot.
seoTitle: Product Usage Scoring & Routing | GTM Systems Project
seoDescription: An explainable weekly Sales and Customer Success routing system that separates fit, product usage, and buying intent, then syncs one approved action to HubSpot.
role: System design, full-stack build, and Cloudflare deployment
constraints: HubSpot writes must be fictional, idempotent, and bounded: one designated account, follow-up tasks only, no email, and no portal or owner secrets exposed.
The weekly queue must stay explainable: it separates fit, product usage, and buying intent instead of collapsing them into one opaque score.
problem: Product behavior often exists, but the weekly Sales and Customer Success queue arrives late, noisy, over capacity, or unexplained. One combined score collapses fit, product value, and buying intent into a single opaque number, so the team cannot tell why an account was routed or who should act.
Without a bounded, explainable routing policy, an account can qualify for human action yet be deferred silently, and Sales or Customer Success can act without an SLA or a record of what changed.
Any real sync to HubSpot carries risk: duplicate tasks, outreach by mistake, or exposing portal and owner details, so the demonstration had to keep writes idempotent, fictional, and clearly bounded.
solution: Designed and built an explainable weekly routing application that scores each account on three separate dimensions — fit, product usage, and buying intent — and applies visible gates before any human action.
Compared the same 120 synthetic accounts under a naive combined score and an explainable gated policy at the same weekly capacity, making the difference legible.
Shipped an account decision packet that shows identity, product-event timeline, scores, gates, rejected alternatives, owner, SLA, and CRM state.
Let visitors adjust two allowlisted levers, the acquisition intent minimum and weekly human-action capacity, then recompute the queue live.

Built a bounded HubSpot sync that idempotently creates one fictional follow-up task, never outreach, through a durable Cloudflare workflow, with a fake local adapter for the demo and a hardened production path.

Ran the whole system on Cloudflare Workers, D1, and Workflows with TanStack Start, validated all boundary data at runtime, and covered the scoring and routing logic with a table-tested decision engine.
result: The demonstration makes the weekly Sales and CS routing decision visible: the same 120 accounts produce different, explainable outcomes under the gated policy and the naive comparator.
Visitors can inspect a single account's decision packet to see exactly which signals, gates, and thresholds routed it, and can change intent or capacity to watch who enters or leaves the queue.
One approved action can synchronize into a real HubSpot developer test account as a fictional task — idempotently, with no outreach and no private portal or owner details exposed.
deliveryHighlights: An explainable weekly Sales and CS routing queue comparing a gated policy and a naive combined score on 120 synthetic accounts
Per-account decision packets showing scores, gates, rejected alternatives, owner, SLA, and CRM state
Adjustable acquisition intent and weekly capacity levers with live queue recompute
A bounded, idempotent HubSpot task sync (never outreach) through a durable Cloudflare workflow
